subject: Tenant key scoping, escrow fallback, and TLS cipher negotiation
messages:
From: Alison Murray <alison.murray@healthgrid.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: dpo@healthgrid.com, security@healthgrid.com
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification: tenant key scoping / escrow fallback / TLS policy

Jonas —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP packet. We have one set of follow-ups before we submit to procurement:

1) Tenant key scoping: Can Redwood restrict cryptographic material such that each HealthGrid tenant has a unique master key that is never accessible in plaintext to Redwood staff or infrastructure? We want to ensure that cross-tenant key derivation is impossible and audit logs show per-tenant key ops.

2) Escrow/fallback: In cases where a customer-managed HSM BYOK import needs to be recovered (lost HSM, legal process), what is Redwood's recommended escrow approach? Do you support dual-control HSM escrow (split-wrapped key material) or only a vendor HSM export? We need details on who can ever decrypt escrow material and under what governance.

3) TLS parameterization: Our security team wants to lock TLS ciphers to a known-good list. What TLS versions/cipher suites does Redwood accept on both client-facing endpoints and internal service-to-service connections? Do you support mTLS to the extent of client certificate pinning per-tenant?

We attached our KMS appendix for context. Please limit answers to what you already support versus roadmap items.

- Alison
Alison Murray
Sr. Security Architect, HealthGrid

Attachments: healthgrid_kms_appendix_v3.pdf (PDF)
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alison Murray <alison.murray@healthgrid.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: tenant key scoping / escrow fallback / TLS policy

Alison —

Appreciate the detailed questions; below is a concise statement of current capabilities and operational constraints. I’ve attached a brief key lifecycle diagram and our KMS capabilities extract for your pack.

1) Tenant key scoping (what we support today)
- Per-tenant root keys: Redwood supports per-tenant master keys via envelope encryption. Each tenant has a tenant_root_key (TRK) that is scoped and versioned; TRKs are stored only as KMS-wrapped blobs.
- No plaintext access by Redwood: TRKs are generated or imported into a customer-managed HSM (PKCS#11 import) or created in-cloud KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure) as customer-managed keys. The runtime only receives envelope keys (data keys) derived and wrapped by the TRK; Redwood processes never materialize master keying material in host memory as plaintext.
- Logical separation: Key metadata includes tenant_id bindings and key_policy documents; operations are audited and IAM-scoped so cross-tenant key operations are prohibited by policy and enforced by the control plane.

2) Escrow / fallback (supported patterns and governance)
- Recommended model: dual-control HSM escrow using a customer-controlled HSM (preferred) or Redwood-managed escrow with HSM sealed blobs under split-wrap governance. We support two patterns:
  a) Customer Escrow Only: Customer maintains an offline HSM/escrow; Redwood will import keys under customer instruction and will not retain an exportable plaintext copy. Recovery requires customer participation.
  b) Managed Escrow (optional): If you opt-in, Redwood can hold an HSM-wrapped escrow blob where the blob is wrapped under two keys: one in the customer KMS/HSM and one in Redwood's escrow HSM. Recovery requires both parties (dual control) to perform an unwrapping ceremony.
- Controls: Managed escrow is subject to written SOPs, notarized access approvals, and an auditable key-release workflow (ticket + 2-person approval + recorded attestation). We involve our Security Operations and the customer DPO for any recovery event.
- No routine exports: We do not export private keying material from customer-managed HSMs unless explicitly requested and performed under the escrow workflow above.

3) TLS parameterization (client-facing and internal)
- Client-facing endpoints: We require TLS 1.2 minimum but recommend and default to TLS 1.3. Accepted cipher suites for public endpoints (TLS 1.3): TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256. For TLS 1.2 we permit ECDHE-ECDSA and ECDHE-RSA with AES-GCM; we disable RSA key-exchange and CBC-mode ciphers by default.
- Internal service-to-service: By default we use mTLS with mutual authentication between control-plane components. Internal links support TLS 1.2/1.3 and AEAD suites; customers can request stricter policies for Private deployments.
- Per-tenant mTLS: For Dedicated and Private modes we support per-tenant client cert pinning at the gateway level. For hosted endpoints, we offer token-based authentication coupled with regional IP allowlists; mTLS per-tenant is available on Dedicated/Private (requires provisioning of tenant certs).

Limitations and timeline notes:
- We currently support PKCS#11 imports for on-prem HSMs and Cloud KMS CMKs for envelope wrapping. A fully managed multi-party HSM escrow product with on-demand hardware escrow retrieval is available as a Professional Services add-on (existing customers can pilot).
- Audit artifacts: All unwrap/wrap events are recorded with non-repudiable logs and per-event attestation signed by our HSM (where applicable).

Next steps: If HealthGrid prefers Managed Escrow, I can send a scope addendum and a draft SOP for the dual-control key release ceremony. Otherwise, for Customer Escrow Only we'll provide the import playbook and PKCS#11 config snippets.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Head of Product Security, Redwood Inference

Attachments: hg_rfp_kms_requirements.pdf (PDF), proposed_key-lifecycle-diagram.svg (SVG)
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: follow-ups on cipher lists and escrow details

Jonas — quick tech notes to include if we get pushed on edge cases by HealthGrid security: 

- Cipher hardening: call out TLS 1.3-only posture as an option for HealthGrid if they control client fleet (reduces attack surface). Also mention TLS AAD record size protections and anti-replay window hygiene for long-lived connections.
- Escrow key metadata: make explicit that escrow blobs are HSM-attested (HSM signs a measurement) and that we record the associated nonce/counters so any later unwrap can be correlated to the original import event.
- Rotation cadence: recommend default TRK rotation annually with immediate emergency rotation triggers. We should provide migration helpers to rewrap data keys and a non-disruptive dual-key window to avoid downtime.

I'll add a short appendix with example PKCS#11 commands and a sample HSM attestation envelope. Monica, can you draft the SOP snippet for the dual-control ceremony (ticket, 2 approvers, external notary)?

— Karthik

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alison Murray <alison.murray@healthgrid.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: tenant key scoping / escrow fallback / TLS policy

Alison —

Thanks for the quick review. Per follow-up internal notes, two clarifications:

• We can offer a TLS 1.3-only posture for HealthGrid for client fleets you control; we will document the impact to any legacy integrations.
• Managed Escrow always includes HSM attestation artifacts (signed measurement + provenance) and a recorded, auditable release path requiring customer sign-off plus Redwood two-person approval.

If you’re comfortable with Managed Escrow as an option, I’ve shared an addendum via DocuSign with the recovery governance and timeline for a pilot. The link is below. If you prefer Customer-Only escrow, we’ll send the PKCS#11 import playbook and a 1-week onboarding schedule for key imports.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/tx/XYZ-HealthGrid-KMS-Addendum
Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cHG-RFP-HG-2027

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk the team through the ceremony; propose Mon 10:00–10:30 PT next week.

Best,
Jonas
Head of Product Security, Redwood Inference
